notes.7: The first heading under which candidates had to write required them to come up with two points about why Gunjan took her children to the parlour. The correct answer was: ‘Because Gunjan did not want her children should be indifferent towards their looks, and wanted her son to stand out in the party’. Most of the candidates gave two correct answers.
notes.8: In order to attract children to the parlour what kinds of activities are organised? Several candidates wrote the correct answer and only very few wrote about the services the parlour offers rather than about the actual activities.
notes.9: This heading was about the negative effects that such activities can have on children. The majority of candidates were able to give the right answers under this heading. Question 10 was about giving two negative factors related to reality shows. The correct answers were: ‘young girls behave like women’, ‘objectification of women’ and ‘young boys and girls are spending more time in beauty parlours’. Most of the candidates gave these answers correctly. Exercise 4 Question 11 In this summary-writing exercise up to six marks are available for Content and four marks for Language. This year most candidates appear to be well-prepared for the requirements of this exercise and generally performed well. Many candidates wrote their summaries in their own words and were therefore able to access the full range of marks available for Language. Most of the candidates wrote precisely, covering five or six correct points from the text. They also managed to secure three out of four marks for language; a few candidates scored full marks for language. The majority of the candidates restricted their answer to within the word limit. However, a small minority of candidates still exceeded the word limit. Section 2 Exercise 5 Questions 12–18 This text was about a village named Patna after the same name city in the state of Bihar in India. This village was named by a Scottish man who came to the city Patna in India as a businessman and when he returned to Scotland then he named his village Patna too. Many of the candidates performed very well in this exercise. All four questions ( Questions 12–15 ) with true/false options (and supplying the correct statement for the false option) were answered correctly by most of the candidates. A minority of candidates gave an incorrect reply to Question 15 as ‘true’, when this statement was false. From Questions 16–18 , most of the candidates gave accurate statements. A few candidates gave an incorrect reply to Question 16 because the word for commodity in Hindi ‘ padarth ’ was not understood Exercise 6 This year’s essay topic was about the link between a healthy mind and a healthy lifestyle. Most of the candidates attempted the exercise successfully. Several candidates gave positive reasons to support the topic. Good answers also gave negative reasons including spending too much time on computers and not making time for exercise or not eating healthy food. Like last year, spelling errors were the main reason for loss of marks. Firstly, the use of the vowel sounds ‘Ee’ was used wrongly. Secondly, the aspirated letters were written with non-aspirated letters in Hindi. Thirdly, the conjunct in Hindi especially with the letter ‘Ra’ was not used correctly. Teachers should encourage their students to think in Hindi because some of the sentence constructions were written in Hindi however it sounded as if students were planning what they were writing in English and then translating their thoughts into Hindi causing problems with the syntax of their writing. For example, some candidates used the word in Hindi for ‘clever’ whereas the same word has a negative connotation in Hindi which was not appropriate in the context in which it was used. HINDI AS A SECOND LANGUAGE
notes.key_messages: ● In Exercises 1 , 3 and 5 the emphasis is on reading skills. Spelling errors are tolerated provided they do not interfere with the communication of the correct answer. Candidates are not required to write in full sentences to score the marks so long as the answer they give is clear. ● In Exercise 2 , complete accuracy is required when filling in the person’s contact details. ● In Exercise 4 and Exercise 6 marks are awarded not only for content but also for accuracy of language. Therefore, it is important that candidates check their work carefully for spelling and grammatical errors.
notes.general_comments: Most of the candidates performed well in this year’s examination. The candidates followed the guidelines appropriately and most of them had written their answers within the word limit. The majority of candidates appeared to be comfortable with the requirements of Exercises 1 , 2 , 3, 4 and 5 .
